title: Fish eDNA Water Sampling and Filtration Protocol
author: Marine Vautier
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.br5rm856

steps.title: Collect water sample
steps.instruction: Put on gloves and open the bottle without touching the cap or neck; collect subsurface water 10–20 cm below the surface by hand; close the bottle carefully; if sampling deeper with a tank, decontaminate the tank before sampling; store the bottle in cleaned containers and keep samples in a cooler during transport.

substeps.instruction: Don gloves.
Open bottle without contacting cap or neck.
Collect water 10–20 cm below surface.
Close bottle carefully.
Decontaminate sampling tank if used for deeper collection.
Place bottle in cleaned container.
Use a cooler if samples must be transported.

steps.title: Store sample before filtration
steps.instruction: Place the collected water at 4 °C in the dark and proceed to filtration within a maximum of 6 hours.

steps.title: Syringe filtration (field)
steps.instruction: Prepare gloves, a Sterivex cartridge with caps, and a 60 mL syringe; remove syringe and Sterivex from blister packs without touching filter ends; gently homogenize the sample and fill the syringe (ensure bottle neck is larger than syringe diameter); connect syringe to Sterivex (Luer‑Lock) and slowly filter the water; when the syringe empties, detach, refill, and continue filtering with the same Sterivex until the desired volume (0.5–5 L) is reached, noting the final volume (initial minus remaining); complete filtration within 1 hour; after filtration, detach Sterivex and remove remaining water by inserting the syringe plunger and passing air through the cartridge.

substeps.instruction: Gather gloves, Sterivex cartridge, caps, and 60 mL syringe.
Remove syringe and Sterivex from blister packs, avoiding contact with filter ends.
Gently homogenize sample and fill syringe (60 mL).
Connect syringe to Sterivex (Luer‑Lock).
Slowly filter water through Sterivex.
When syringe is empty, detach, refill, and continue filtering with the same Sterivex.
Record final filtered volume (initial volume minus remaining volume).
Ensure total filtration time does not exceed 1 hour.
Detach Sterivex and remove residual water by inserting plunger and passing air through the cartridge.

steps.title: Vacuum‑pump filtration (lab)
steps.instruction: Prepare gloves, vacuum pump, tubing, a filter ramp sized for the Sterivex, caps, and a 50 mL syringe; remove Sterivex from blister pack without touching filter ends; insert the Male Luer‑lock outlet tip into a clean silicone filter support holder and place the holder onto the filtration ramp; remove the plunger from the 50 mL syringe and use the body as a funnel; connect the syringe body to the Female Luer‑lock inlet tip of the Sterivex; gently homogenize the sample and slowly fill the syringe directly from the bottle; switch on the pump, open valves, and keep pressure ≤ 400 mBa (40 kPa); keep the syringe filled with water and continue filtration with the same Sterivex until 0.5–5 L is filtered, noting the final volume; complete filtration within 1 hour; after filtration, disconnect Sterivex from the holder and remove remaining water by inserting the plunger and passing air through the cartridge.

substeps.instruction: Gather gloves, vacuum pump, tubing, filter ramp, caps, and 50 mL syringe.
Remove Sterivex from blister pack, avoiding contact with filter ends.
Insert Male Luer‑lock outlet tip into clean silicone filter support holder.
Place holder onto the filtration ramp.
Remove plunger from syringe; use syringe body as funnel.
Connect syringe body to Female Luer‑lock inlet tip of Sterivex.
Gently homogenize sample and slowly fill syringe directly from bottle.
Turn on pump, open valves, and ensure pressure does not exceed 400 mBa (40 kPa).
Maintain water in syringe and continue filtration until desired volume (0.5–5 L) is reached, recording final volume.
Limit total filtration time to ≤ 1 hour.
Disconnect Sterivex from holder and remove residual water by inserting plunger and passing air through the cartridge.

steps.title: Preserve filtered sample
steps.instruction: Gather buffer, a 1000 µL pipette or 5 mL syringe, an indelible marker or pre‑printed label, a sterile bag or tube, field sheet and pen; place the outlet cap on the Sterivex; add exactly 2 mL of buffer using the pipette tip (or 5 mL syringe) inserted well into the cartridge to avoid overflow; place the inlet cap on the Sterivex; label the cartridge and store it in a clean bag/tube; store at room temperature for several hours, in a fridge or cooler for a few days, or at –20 °C for longer periods; complete the field sheet.

substeps.instruction: Prepare buffer, 1000 µL pipette or 5 mL syringe, marker/label, sterile bag or tube, field sheet, and pen.
Place outlet cap on Sterivex.
Add 2 mL of buffer using pipette tip (or 5 mL syringe), inserting tip well to prevent overflow.
Place inlet cap on Sterivex.
Label Sterivex and place it in a clean bag/tube.
Store at room temperature (several hours), fridge/cooler (few days), or –20 °C for longer storage.
Complete the field sheet.
